Concurrent jobs sharing the work directory raced via tmp_path.replace, leaving training reading partially-written or shuffled indices. Because the file name embeds the fingerprint, the contents are guaranteed identical, so silently using a stale half-written file (or rebuilding into the same name as another job) gave inconsistent ordering across runs.
trigger_conditions: Multiple training jobs share the same work_dir
SamplingInstanceSource used; rank-0 builds the cached indices file

title: memmap_to_write tmp filename uses seeded random — concurrent writers collide on identical path under the same RNG seed
root_cause: memmap_to_write picked the temp filename via random.randint(0, 2**32) seeded by the global Python RNG. With identical seeds across ranks, each rank generated the same tmp_path; one rank's tmp_path.replace removed the file another rank was about to read, causing FileNotFoundError-style silent data shadowing or partial-content reads when a fallback masked the error.
trigger_conditions: Multiple ranks/processes preprocess the same path with the same global random seed

title: MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel falls back to default group when dist is unavailable but never wires per-bucket grad reduce
root_cause: MoE-style parameters were reduced one-by-one through the existing DDP path, missing the view-based bucket optimization that batches grads of the same dtype/process_group into a single all-reduce. Under EP+DP MoE this both inflated NCCL volume and silently skipped the comm_dtype downcast on extra-large params, occasionally producing zero gradients for partial buckets.
trigger_conditions: MoE-shaped parameters require per-bucket grad reduction with view-based storage

title: Mamba.forward casts inputs using cached self.dtype — wrong dtype after FSDP wraps the conv1d weight
root_cause: Mamba.forward used self.dtype (snapshot at construction time) to cast x. After FSDP wrapped the inner conv1d, the actual parameter dtype changed but self.dtype was stale, so x flowed into the kernel in the wrong precision. The MambaSSM kernel still ran but produced silently wrong values.
trigger_conditions: Mamba sequence mixer wrapped in FSDP / FSDP2
Mixed-precision params (e.g., bf16 weights, fp32 cast targets)

title: DTPBoundaryPredictor calls F.silu with two arguments — silu treats w3(h) as inplace flag, drops gating
root_cause: The expression F.silu(self.w1(h), self.w3(h)) passed self.w3(h) as the inplace argument of F.silu (PyTorch interprets the second positional as a bool-coerced inplace flag). The intended SwiGLU gate (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)) never executed, so the FFN computed silu(w1(h)) alone and the boundary predictor produced silently degraded outputs.
trigger_conditions: BLT DTPBoundaryPredictor used for byte-level training

title: sqrt decay LR schedule uses wrong formula — decay curve inverted
root_cause: sqrt(progress) instead of 1-sqrt(1-progress) — wrong decay curve shape

title: MoE sigmoid router gives F.sigmoid(logits) without epsilon — exact-zero scores propagate as NaN through downstream log
root_cause: scores = F.sigmoid(logits) could underflow to exactly 0.0 under low precision, and downstream load-balancing or aux-loss code took log/divide of the score, producing -inf/NaN that silently propagated into the final loss without any explicit error.
trigger_conditions: Highly negative logits causing sigmoid output ~ 0 in bf16/fp16

title: fused_linear_cross_entropy_loss accumulates gradient in bf16 by default — silently noisier than fp32 accumulation
root_cause: The liger-kernel fused linear+CE call defaulted accum_grad to bf16, which silently degraded gradient precision on the LM head. The numerical noise was small enough that training continued, but it shifted loss curves vs the unfused baseline.

title: fan_in init for embeddings ignores embed_scale — embeddings remain std=1.0 and become huge after scaling
root_cause: init_embeddings under fan_in always used std=1.0. The transformer then multiplied embeddings by embed_scale (e.g., sqrt(d_model)) at the input, producing embeddings several orders of magnitude larger than intended. Training did not error but the input magnitude scrambled the early-layer dynamics.
trigger_conditions: Transformer config sets embed_scale (e.g., Gemma-like models)

title: Evaluator iterates with stale data-loader state — second eval pass starts mid-stream, evaluating a different subset
root_cause: Evaluator.__iter__ called reshuffle() but did not reset() the data loader. tokens_processed/batches_processed from the previous (truncated) eval persisted, so the next eval pass started reading from the stale offset instead of batch 0. Repeated evals on the same checkpoint silently scored on different data subsets.
trigger_conditions: LM evaluator runs multiple passes with eval_duration truncating each pass
DataLoaderBase carried over batches_processed from the previous pass

title: Trainer async bookkeeping callback fires after future is FINISHED — state_dict snapshot can capture pre-callback state
root_cause: _run_bookkeeping_op attached cb via future.add_done_callback. add_done_callback runs after the future is marked FINISHED, so _join_bookkeeping_ops returned before cb ran, and a state_dict() capture immediately after could observe stale callback state (e.g., un-rotated checkpoint indexes).
trigger_conditions: Trainer launches a bookkeeping op (e.g., async checkpoint save) that has a completion cb

title: Grad clipper recorded grad_norm DTensor — record_metric saw distributed value
root_cause: GradClipperCallback recorded the raw grad_norm output from torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ without unwrapping it. With TP, this returned a DTensor; the metric system then operated on the DTensor across ranks, producing a wrongly reduced grad-norm value while clipping itself was already applied locally.

title: NaN loss when all instances on a rank are masked — division by zero
root_cause: batch_num_tokens_for_loss = 0 when all instances masked, causing loss / 0 = NaN

title: Instance filter loss divisor missed masked-out instance tokens — wrong gradient scale
root_cause: When the instance filter dropped instances on some ranks the loss divisor (batch_num_tokens_for_loss) only counted unmasked tokens. With per-rank sum-then-allreduce, ranks with fewer kept tokens contributed an artificially large per-token loss, producing an unfair weighted average across the data-parallel group and a wrong gradient magnitude.

title: SkipStepOptimizer fed unreduced ce_batch_loss — skip decisions on per-rank values
root_cause: SkipStepOptimizer.latest_loss was set from the local per-rank ce_batch_loss before the all-reduce that produced the global mean. The rolling-window statistics for outlier detection were thus computed on per-rank loss values, and skip-step decisions diverged across ranks, producing inconsistent optimizer behavior.

title: Mamba2 ladder hard-coded head_dim from d_model/n_heads — wrong with FLA defaults
root_cause: The ladder configurators forced fla_layer_kwargs={'head_dim': ensure_multiple_of(d_model/n_heads, 128)}. FLA's Mamba2 already derives head_dim from its own internal layout, so injecting an externally-rounded value made the constructed Mamba2 layer disagree with the configured d_model/n_heads, producing a model whose effective head dimension differed from what other code assumed.

title: BLT byte embeddings never initialized to teacher-embedding stats — kept default kaiming
root_cause: fix_init computed te_mean and te_std of the target embeddings but used them only when initializing hash_embeddings; the main self.embedding.weight (byte embeddings) was never assigned the te-scaled init, leaving it at nn.Embedding's default initialization. The encoder therefore started training with byte embeddings whose distribution did not match the teacher's vocabulary embeddings.
trigger_conditions: BLT distill training with target_embeddings provided

title: Flex-attention sliding-window mask used Python `and` on tensors — short-circuit returned wrong mask
root_cause: _get_flex_attn_mask_mod._sliding_window_mask_mod returned `q_idx - kv_idx <= window_size[0] and kv_idx - q_idx <= window_size[1]`. Python's `and` calls bool() on the first operand and short-circuits — for scalar bool tensors this returns the second operand whenever the first is truthy and the first when falsy, never producing the intended logical AND. The mask was therefore computed as a single one-sided comparison.

title: BLT stage1 froze only teacher.* — student blocks updated against teacher gradient
root_cause: freeze_params=['teacher.*'] only matched submodules named 'teacher.*'. Because share_blocks_between_teacher_and_student=True, the actual block parameters live under 'blocks.*' (shared with teacher); those weren't matched by the freeze pattern, so blocks were unfrozen and trained against gradients that included contributions from the teacher path.
trigger_conditions: shared blocks between teacher and student

title: Document packing sort overflow — uint32 * -1 wraps to huge positive
freeze_experts assigned in __init__ instead of dataclass field — OmegaConf merge dropped it
root_cause: FreezeTransformerTrainModuleConfig set self.freeze_experts via kwargs.pop in __init__ rather than declaring it as a dataclass field. Config.merge serializes/reconstructs through OmegaConf, which drops fields that aren't declared dataclass attributes; freeze_experts always reverted to the default 'first_half' regardless of the user's configured value, silently zeroing the first half of router gradients.
trigger_conditions: any CLI override applied via Config.merge

title: MultiHeadLatentAttention init dispatched to Attention branch — wrong layers initialized
root_cause: InitMethod.init_attention dispatched on isinstance(m, Attention) before isinstance hasattr(m, 'wq_a'). Because MultiHeadLatentAttention inherits from Attention and exposes w_q, the MLA branch was never reached; the projections wq_a, wkv_a, wkv_b were never initialized while only w_q was, leaving the rest at the dtype-empty allocation values.

title: Qwen3Clone-8B script forgot use_head_qk_norm — used per-channel QK norm instead of per-head
root_cause: build_model_config for Qwen3Clone-8B configured the Qwen3 model but did not set config.block.attention.use_head_qk_norm = True. Qwen3 uses per-head QK norm; the default per-channel QK norm was applied instead, normalizing across the wrong axis and producing different attention scores from the reference Qwen3.

title: H-Net ratio loss averaged over padded positions — wrong target ratio under variable-length batches
root_cause: true_ratio = boundary_mask.float().mean() and average_prob = exp(boundary_logprobs).mean() averaged over the full padded byte tensor instead of over byte_mask-valid positions. Padded zero entries shrank both quantities toward 0, biasing the ratio loss target away from the true content ratio.

title: H-Net embed loss never normalized by loss_div_factor — wrong loss weighting
root_cause: The BLTDistillTransformer finalize block called self._finalize_loss on local_encoder_loss and local_decoder_loss but omitted the call for hnet_embed_loss. The component was added to the weighted-sum loss as a raw sum (not divided by token count), so its effective weight was inflated by approximately seq_len * batch_size relative to the configured loss_weights entry.

title: BLTDistill patch loss div factor used input_ids.numel() — wrong scaling for byte-level losses
root_cause: The byte-level loss div factor was computed as loss_div_factor / input_ids.numel(), but loss_div_factor passed in is at the byte sequence level not the patch level. The correct denominator is h_byte.shape[0] * h_byte.shape[1] (number of byte positions), and the patch loss needs an analogous division by patch positions. The mismatch silently mis-weighted byte vs patch loss components.

title: Flex attention not upcast to fp32 — precision mismatch with SDPA backend
root_cause: Flex attention was called directly on bf16 q/k/v while SDPA's reference path runs the matmul/softmax in fp32. The bf16-only flex path silently produced lower-precision attention outputs that diverge from the SDPA path used by tests, causing different loss trajectories between the two backends.

title: Sliding window size off-by-one — window 1 token too small
BLT distill missed first-call label_offsets when fuse_boundaries enabled
root_cause: The label-offset application path that conditionally adds vocab_size_blt to boundary positions was duplicated for the alternate boundary computation but missed in the first forward branch. Boundary positions did not get their offsets applied to labels, so the cross-entropy compared against the wrong target indices for boundary tokens.

title: BLT shift_boundary_mask did not AND with byte_mask — pad positions polluted label offsets
root_cause: shift_boundary_mask was computed as boundary_mask[:, 1:] without AND-ing with byte_mask[:, 1:]. Padded positions where boundary_mask happened to be True (left-over from a previous batch slot) added vocab_size_blt//2 to label entries that should have remained at the ignore_index, distorting CE on padded positions.
trigger_conditions: padded byte positions present in batch

title: SourceMixtureDataset rounded down per-source instances — dataset shorter than expected
root_cause: tokens_requested_per_path = ceil(target_ratio * num_tokens_in_path) and instances_requested_per_path = tokens_requested_per_path // sequence_length. The integer-floor in the second step dropped the per-path remainder, so total instances < training_steps * batch_size. The trainer ran past the end of the dataset into epoch 2 with no warning — visible only as an unexpected loss drop near end of run.

title: FSLDataset fingerprint missed sequence_length / bos_token_id — wrong cache reused
root_cause: fingerprint_fields for several FSLDataset variants did not include sequence_length, bos_token_id, max_target_sequence_length. Cached instance offsets / packed indices computed under the previous values were reused when those settings changed, so the dataset returned instances whose actual layout no longer matched the configured sequence_length.
trigger_conditions: NumpyPaddedFSLDataset / NumpyPackedFSLDataset / NumpyInterleavedFSLDataset cached on disk
subsequent run with different sequence_length/bos_token_id but matching pre-existing fingerprint

title: DataCollator routed academic/technical sources to a non-existent 4th expert label
root_cause: _source_name_to_expert_label produced a one-hot at index 3 for academic/technical sources, but the deployed model only had 3 active experts (indices 0..2 plus a masked duplicate). The label tensor pointed to an unused expert slot, so router supervision was silently directed to a slot the router never produced gradient for.
trigger_conditions: FlexOLMo SFT with expert routing labels

title: PoE z_loss combined into combined_loss is detached, contributing value but no gradient
root_cause: In TransformerTrainModule.train_batch the PoE branch added output.z_loss to combined_loss, but LMHead emits output.z_loss as a detached metric tensor. The optimizer therefore saw the z_loss value in the printed metric while backprop applied zero z_loss gradient, so logit-norm regularization never actually constrained the weights.
